# AMZN — Technical Analysis Report (as of 2024-02-06)

**Verified snapshot values (source of truth).** All price and indicator figures below come from the frozen-row snapshot and the indicator histories for AMZN; they reconcile exactly with each other (no conflicts to flag).

- Latest session (2024-02-06): **O 169.39 / H 170.71 / L 167.65 / C 169.15**, volume **42.51M**
- Prior two sessions: 2024-02-02 C **171.81** (H 172.50, volume **117.22M**), 2024-02-05 C **170.31** (volume 55.08M)
- 2024-02-01 close (pre-news) **159.28**, high **159.76**

---

## 1. The dominant event: a post-earnings gap that is so far holding

The single most important feature on the chart is the **2024-02-02 gap**: AMZN opened at **169.19** versus the prior close of **159.28** and closed at **171.81** — a **+7.87% close-to-close move** with **117.2M shares** traded (roughly 2.3–2.5× the ~45–50M typical January session; it is the largest volume print since the 125.3M of 2023-10-27, though below the 153.1M of 2023-08-04). This was the Q4-2023 earnings reaction, and the structure it created matters more than the percentage itself:

- **Unfilled gap zone: 159.76 → 167.33** (between the 2024-02-01 high and the 2024-02-02 low). That is a 7.57-point void equal to **4.7%** of the pre-gap price.
- Since the gap, price has built **two inside sessions** (170.31, then 169.15) with highs of 170.55 and 170.71 — i.e. **no attempt to close the gap**, and the whole consolidation sits **entirely above the gap top (167.33)**.
- Volume has **decayed** across those two sessions (117.2M → 55.1M → 42.5M). Pullback/consolidation on **contracting** volume after an expansion day is the textbook healthy signature; distribution would show expanding down-volume.
- Short-term caution: the last three closes (171.81 → 170.31 → 169.15) and the last two highs (172.50 → 170.55/170.71) form a mild **lower-high/lower-close drift**. It is shallow (<2% off the high) and occurring at the top of the range, which is stalling rather than reversal behaviour — but it does argue against chasing strength at 169–172.

**Reference high:** 172.50 (2024-02-02 intraday) is the highest print in the entire 2023-08-01 → 2024-02-06 window; the highest close is 171.81. From that high, the current 169.15 is only **−1.94%**.

---

## 2. Trend structure: bullish and *accelerating*, but extended

| Metric | 2024-02-06 | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Close | 169.15 | — |
| 10 EMA | **163.11** | Price 3.7% above; the 10 EMA has turned up hard (157.22 on 02-01 → 163.11 on 02-06) |
| 50 SMA | **152.54** | Price 10.9% above; rising ~0.45/day |
| 200 SMA | **134.61** | Price 25.7% above; rising ~0.33/day |

- **Stacked, properly ordered averages:** Close (169.15) > 10 EMA (163.11) > 50 SMA (152.54) > 200 SMA (134.61). This is a clean full-bull alignment with no compression anywhere in the stack.
- **50/200 spread is widening**: 142.57 − 127.46 = **15.11** on 2023-12-28 versus 152.54 − 134.61 = **17.93** on 2024-02-06. The 50 SMA sits **13.3%** above the 200 SMA — a long-established (not newly formed) golden-cross regime, which is confirmation of a strategic uptrend rather than a fresh timing signal.
- **The 200 SMA has not been tested since the October 2023 basing**: the swing low close in the dataset is **119.57 (2023-10-26)** — at that point price was *below* the long-term average. From 119.57 to 169.15 is **+41.5%**, and the entire advance since has been one of higher lows: 119.57 (Oct 26) → 144.57 (Jan 4) → 155.20 (Jan 31) → 167.65 (Feb 6).
- **Extension is the main technical negative.** 10.9% above the 50 SMA and 3.7% above the 10 EMA is a stretched posture. Historically this resolves either by (a) sideways time-based consolidation until the averages catch up, or (b) a sharp mean-reversion wick. The Jan 2–4 pullback (149.93 → 144.57, −3.6%) is the most recent example of the latter and it respected nothing more than the 50 SMA area (then 143.94–144.30), which is instructive for where dip-buyers have previously appeared.

---

## 3. Momentum: strongly positive and re-accelerating, with early overbought friction

**MACD (12,26,9):**
- MACD line **4.459**, signal **3.161**, histogram **+1.298** — bullish configuration with an expanding histogram.
- The MACD line bottomed at **0.779 on 2024-01-08** and has since risen to 4.459, i.e. it has more than quintupled. Crucially, it **surged from 2.395 (01-31) to 4.459 (02-06)**, a +86% move in four sessions, driven by the gap. That is momentum *expansion*, not a lagging cross.
- The MACD line is well above its December peak (2.989 on 2023-12-28) even though price is only modestly above December levels — a sign that the *rate of change* has improved, not just the level.

**RSI(14): 68.31**
- Path: **40.23 on 2024-01-04** → 70.41 on 01-29 → 53.10 on 01-31 (pre-earnings flush) → **73.78 on 2024-02-02** (overbought print) → 70.69 → **68.31**.
- Two readings matter. First, the RSI **did not confirm the January price highs**: price made a higher high on 2024-01-29 (close 161.26) than on 2023-12-28 (153.38), yet RSI printed 70.41 versus 63.94 — that is *positive* momentum divergence, and it preceded the gap. Second, the current 68.31 is **below** the 73.78 overbought peak while price is still within 2% of its high — a mild **negative (bearish) divergence** forming at the margin.
- Interpretation: in a strong trend RSI in the high-60s is not a sell signal; it is a "don't add size here" signal. The RSI reset on 01-31 from 70 to 53 in two sessions also proves this name can flush 2–4% quickly without breaking structure.

**MFI (from snapshot): 0.68** (0–1 scale ≈ 68/100) — money-flow strength sits in the same elevated-but-not-extreme zone as RSI, providing mild corroboration that the advance is volume-supported rather than a thin drift. It is not showing its own divergence.

---

## 4. Volatility: ATR regime shift and a band-walk in progress

**ATR(14): 3.836**, or **2.27% of the close**.
- The regime shift is visible in the series: 2.94 (01-29) → 3.16 (02-01) → **3.88 (02-02)** → 3.90 (02-05) → 3.84 (02-06). ATR jumped **+23% in a single session** on the earnings gap and has stayed there. Stops sized on January's ~2.9–3.0 ATR are now too tight for this tape.
- Practical mapping: 1×ATR = 3.84; 1.5×ATR = 5.75; 2×ATR = 7.67. A 2×ATR trailing stop from the 172.50 high sits at **164.83** — above the 10 EMA (163.11) but comfortably below the gap top, which conveniently aligns risk control with structure.

**Bollinger(20,2): middle 157.96 / upper 169.89 / lower 146.03** (bandwidth 15.1% of the middle band).
- Price at 169.15 sits at **~97% of the band range** (%B), i.e. pressed against the upper band. On **2024-02-02 the close of 171.81 was 3.3% ABOVE that day's upper band (166.33)** — a genuine volatility breakout print, not just a touch.
- The upper band is **expanding aggressively** (163.10 on 02-01 → 166.33 → 168.28 → **169.89**), which is the classic signature of a trending, "walking-the-band" market. In this state, band touches are continuation cues, and shorting the upper band is a low-probability trade until the band flattens.
- The failure mode to watch: price **fails to reclaim 170–172 for several sessions while the upper band keeps rising** — then the band rolls over and the mid-band (currently **157.96**, rising ~1.4/day) becomes the magnet. Note the mid-band is *below* the gap top (159.76–167.33), so a full gap fill would roughly coincide with a return to the mean.

---

## 5. Volume / participation: VWMA confirms, and the average buyer is in profit

**VWMA: 160.82** — price is **5.2% above** it, and the VWMA is climbing steeply: 150.70 (2023-12-29) → 156.42 (02-01) → **158.79 (02-02)** → 159.89 → 160.82. That is a +2.03 jump on the gap day, the largest single-day VWMA advance in the window, confirming that the breakout occurred on real volume-weighted participation rather than a low-liquidity drift.

Why this matters practically: **the volume-weighted cost basis of recent buyers (~160.8) is 5.2% below spot**. That cohort is in profit, which supports the idea that dips toward 161–163 will be bought, but it also means there is an obvious cluster of late-December/January longs whose break-even sits right at the **gap top / VWMA zone (159.8–160.8)** — a natural place for supply to re-appear if the gap starts to fail.

---

---

## 7. Actionable interpretation & trade construction

**Bias: bullish trend continuation, but not at market.** The evidence is overwhelming on trend (stacked averages, widening 50/200 spread, MACD expansion, VWMA confirmation, band walk) and mildly cautionary on timing (RSI 68, 10.9% above the 50 SMA, 97%B, three declining closes).

1. **Preferred entry: buy the pullback, not the print.** The 163–161 zone (10 EMA 163.11 and VWMA 160.82) is the highest-quality risk/reward area — it is above the gap top, so the breakout thesis is intact, and it gives roughly 2×ATR of room to the invalidation. Scale in two tranches (≈163 and ≈161).
2. **Breakout continuation entry:** a daily close above **172.50** on volume >50M re-asserts upside momentum with target discovery above the dataset's high; use 167.3–168.0 (gap-day low / rising upper band) as the stop reference, i.e. ~4.5 points ≈ 1.2×ATR — tight, so size accordingly.
3. **Stop discipline:** the thesis is *structurally* wrong below **159.76** (gap top). Anyone long from here should accept a stop in the **159.5–161.5** band (1.0–1.25×ATR below the 163/161 entries). A close inside the 159.76–167.33 gap converts the setup from "breakaway gap" to "exhaustion/ordinary gap," and the base case shifts to the mid-band at **157.96**.
4. **Take-profit / trim logic:** trim partial size if RSI pushes above ~75 **while the MACD histogram contracts** (currently expanding at 1.298, so no such signal yet). First objective is a test of 172.50; a measured continuation beyond that projects to the high-170s given the 7.6-point gap and 15.1% band width, but treat that as scenario, not forecast.
5. **Position sizing:** with ATR at 2.27% of price, a 1% account-risk per trade implies a position sized on a ~6–8 point stop, i.e. materially smaller than a January-volatility sizing model would have allowed (ATR was ~2.9 then, 3.8 now).
6. **Do not fade the upper band.** The 02-02 close above the upper band by 3.3% plus 117M volume is a volatility-expansion signal. Mean-reversion shorts against a walking band have poor odds until (a) the band flattens and (b) a close occurs back below the 10 EMA.

**Two-sided watch list:** *Invalidation of the near-term bull case* = close below 167.33 followed by a failure to reclaim, or a MACD histogram flip negative (currently +1.298, so monitor daily). *Confirmation of continuation* = a higher high above 172.50 accompanied by volume returning above ~55–60M, with RSI making a matching new high (which would erase the nascent negative divergence).

---

# AMZN — Fundamental Research Report
**As of 2024-02-06 | Company: Amazon.com, Inc. | Latest public filing in dataset: FY2023 Form 10-K accepted 2024-02-02 (accession 0001018724-24-000008)**

---

## 1. What is new and why it matters (point-in-time)

The single most important fact for a trader on 2024-02-06 is that **Amazon's fiscal 2023 Form 10-K hit EDGAR on 2024-02-02**, i.e. four days before today's date. Every figure below is post-print and reflects the first full audited look at FY2023 (year ended 2023-12-31). Nothing in this dataset pre-dates that filing in a way that is stale — the FY2021/FY2022 comparatives are restated as presented within the same FY2023 10-K, so they are internally consistent.

Three facts define the FY2023 story:
1. **Free cash flow flipped from deeply negative to strongly positive** ($32.2B in FY2023 vs. –$16.9B in FY2022).
2. **Operating margin expanded ~400bp to 6.4%**, driven by cost-of-sales leverage, not by cutting the tech/fulfillment bucket.
3. **The balance sheet de-risked**: long-term debt down 13%, zero new long-term issuance, cash + marketable securities of ~$144B against ~$70B of debt and finance leases.

---

## 2. Income statement — revenue and the margin inflection

**Revenue is not a direct tag in this extract, so it is derived and cross-checked:** Revenue = `CostsAndExpenses` + `OperatingIncomeLoss`. This yields $574.785B (FY23), $513.983B (FY22), $469.822B (FY21), which tie exactly to Amazon's reported net sales in the FY2023 10-K. Treat revenue below as derived-but-verified.

| $M | FY2021 | FY2022 | FY2023 | YoY '23 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (derived) | 469,822 | 513,983 | 574,785 | **+11.8%** |
| Cost of goods & services | 272,344 | 288,831 | 304,739 | +5.5% |
| Gross profit | 197,478 | 225,152 | 270,046 | +19.9% |
| Gross margin | 42.0% | 43.8% | **47.0%** | +320bp |
| Total costs & expenses | 444,943 | 501,735 | 537,933 | +7.2% |
| Marketing expense | 32,551 | 42,238 | 44,370 | +5.0% |
| G&A expense | 8,823 | 11,891 | 11,816 | –0.6% |
| Advertising expense (separate tag) | 16,900 | 20,600 | 20,300 | –1.5% |
| **Operating income** | 24,879 | 12,248 | **36,852** | **+200.9%** |
| Operating margin | 5.30% | 2.38% | **6.41%** | +403bp |
| Non-operating income/(expense) | 13,272 | (18,184) | 705 | n.m. |
| Pre-tax income | 38,151 | (5,936) | 37,557 | n.m. |
| Income tax | 4,791 | (3,217) | 7,120 | n.m. |
| **Net income** | 33,364 | (2,722) | **30,425** | n.m. |
| Net margin | 7.10% | –0.53% | **5.29%** | — |
| Diluted EPS | $3.24 | $(0.27) | **$2.90** | n.m. |

**Key structural read-throughs:**

- **Gross margin is the engine.** Cost of sales fell from 58.0% of revenue (FY21) to 56.2% (FY22) to **53.0% (FY23)**. That is ~$12B+ of annualized cost-of-sales leverage — consistent with fulfillment-network regionalization, lower per-unit logistics cost, and the mix contribution of high-margin AWS and advertising.
- **Operating leverage is real, but not from the big bucket.** Total opex ex-COGS was $233.2B = 40.6% of revenue vs. 41.4% in FY22. Marketing grew only 5.0% and G&A was flat/slightly down; the combined "fulfillment + technology & content + other" residual was $177.0B (30.8% of revenue) vs. 30.9% in FY22 — i.e. **flat as a percentage**. So the entire margin gain came from gross margin plus marketing/G&A discipline, while Amazon kept spending on technology/content. This is a durable-quality signal rather than a one-off cost cut.
- **Earnings quality caveat on non-operating lines.** FY2022's pre-tax loss of –$5.9B was overwhelmingly a mark-to-market artifact: equity securities FVNI swung –$13.6B in FY22 vs. +$11.6B in FY21 (the Rivian stake) and +$1.0B in FY23. Strip that out and FY2022 operating performance ($12.2B OI) was weak but profitable. For FY2023, operating income of $36.9B was ~98% of pre-tax income — **clean, operations-driven earnings**.
- **Interest: now near-neutral.** Interest expense $3,182M (FY23 vs. $2,367M) is almost fully offset by interest income $2,949M (vs. $989M). Higher rates are a two-sided exposure; the net drag alongside finance-lease interest ($304M) is small.
- **Tax rate is normalizing upward**: effective rate 12.6% (FY21) → 54.2% (FY22, on a small pre-tax base) → **19.0% FY23** ($7,120M / $37,557M). Deferred tax was still a –$5,876M benefit, and **cash taxes paid were $11,179M** — i.e. cash tax rate ~29.8% of pre-tax book income. Tax is becoming a real cash cost, a headwind to incremental EPS.
- Segments: the 10-K confirms **3 operating segments** (North America, International, AWS); segment-level revenue/operating income is not exposed in this extract.
- Advertising expense line ($20,300M) is a disclosure of Amazon's own ad spend, and it *declined* 1.5% — worth distinguishing from advertising *revenue* (a high-margin segment that this dataset does not break out).

---

## 3. Cash flow — the headline of the print

| $M | FY2021 | FY2022 | FY2023 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operating cash flow | 46,327 | 46,752 | **84,946** (+81.7%) |
| Capex (productive assets) | (61,053) | (63,645) | **(52,729)** (–17.2%) |
| **Free cash flow** | **(14,726)** | **(16,893)** | **+32,217** |
| FCF margin | –3.1% | –3.3% | **+5.6%** |
| Capex / revenue | 13.0% | 12.4% | **9.2%** |
| D&A | 34,433 | 41,921 | 48,663 |
| SBC | 12,757 | 19,621 | **24,023** |
| Investing cash flow | (58,154) | (37,601) | (49,833) |
| Financing cash flow | 6,291 | 9,718 | **(15,879)** |
| FX effect on cash | (364) | (1,093) | 403 |
| Net change in cash | (5,900) | 17,776 | 19,637 |

This is a **~$49B year-over-year swing in free cash flow** — the single strongest fundamental catalyst in the dataset. Two drivers, both structural:
- **Operating cash flow +$38.2B** on higher operating income, higher D&A (+$6.7B), higher SBC (+$4.4B), and working-capital help from deferred revenue (+$4,578M) and payables (+$5,381M). Offsets: receivables/other operating assets a $8,348M use, accrued liabilities a $2,428M use, other non-current assets a $12,265M use.
- **Capex down $10.9B** to $52.7B (9.2% of revenue) while D&A rose to $48.7B — capex/D&A is now **1.08x vs 1.52x in FY2022**, meaning the hyper-investment phase is normalizing and the depreciation tailwind is shrinking toward neutral.

**Intra-year acceleration (derived from 10-Q facts in the same dataset):** 9M2023 OCF was $42,481M; FY2023 OCF $84,946M implies **~$42.5B of operating cash flow was generated in Q4 alone** — roughly equal to the first nine months combined. Likewise 9M capex $38,141M vs. FY $52,729M implies **Q4 capex ~$14.6B** and **Q4-only FCF ~$27.9B**. The quarterly cash trajectory is steeply improving, which is the number the market re-rated on.

**Cash-flow-derived EBITDA proxy** (Operating income + D&A + SBC): $24,879 + 34,433 + 12,757 = $72.1B (15.3% margin) in FY21 → $73.8B (14.4%) in FY22 → **$109.5B (19.1%) in FY23**. Adjusted cash earnings power expanded ~$35.7B in one year.

**Conservative lenses traders should keep handy:**
- FCF less finance-lease principal ($4,384M) = **$27.8B**.
- FCF less all SBC ($24,023M) = **~$8.2B** — the true "shareholder" FCF after compensating employees in stock.
- FCF per share = **$3.10** ($32,217M / 10,383M shares) vs. diluted EPS of $2.90.

---

## 4. Balance sheet — liquidity, leverage and deferred revenue

**Reads:**
- **Net cash position ~$73.9B**: cash + AFS securities $144.3B vs. debt $58.3B + finance leases $12.1B = $70.4B. Even including operating leases ($75.6B liability / $90.8B undiscounted), leverage is comfortable. Note the marketable-securities portfolio is laddered short: **$65.2B matures within one year**, so liquidity is genuinely accessible, not duration-locked (unrealized portfolio loss is de minimis: $71,265M amortized cost vs. $70,919M fair value).
